source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 17,350.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 32,650.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). The federal amount adds 1,600.00 for the listed spouse by the brief's per-person rule; it is given, not tested. No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 50,000.00 + (0.00) = 50,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing separate), worksheet for people 65 or older: 1 box checked (spouse only), 4,120.00 + 1 x 700.00 = 4,820.00 (the worksheet prints 4,820.00); line 5 exemption allowance (1 exemption) 9,160.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 4,820.00 + 9,160.00 = 13,980.00; line 7 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 13,980.00 = 36,020.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 23,000.00 = 1,196.00 + 5.58% x (36,020.00 - 23,000.00 = 13,020.00) = 726.5160; total 1,922.5160 = 1,922.52. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 36,001-36,050, single, head of household or married filing separate column, PDF page 29, gives 1,923; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 1,922.52. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 1,922.52. The worksheet has 'You were 65 or older' and 'Spouse was 65 or older' boxes and prints four-box totals for a separate return (PDF page 6), so a filer of 60 with a spouse of 66 checks one box: 4,820.00. The income is all the filer's. The projection counts age per person, so this agrees only when both people are listed on the case, as here; the settlement log marks this as unsure.
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
